result:
`final.py` is a LIRS cache (a low-recency-set eviction policy) with about 5% of the capacity reserved for resident keys that were not recently reused. It scores 0.565 on the search split, against 0.365 for the baseline.

I used 5 of the 24 scoring calls. My earlier ARC (adaptive recency/frequency) version scored 0.407. The first LIRS try crashed with a `KeyError`, which I fixed.

Per-trace hit rates for the final file:

| Trace | Hit rate |
|---|---|
| `hot_with_scans` | 0.241 |
| `loop_and_hot` | 0.638 |
| `phases` | 0.647 |
| `mixed` | 0.262 |
| `recency` | 0.801 |
| `shifting_loops` | 0.800 |

I also tried 12% and 2% for the reserved share. 12% scored 0.556, and 2% scored 0.567, only marginally higher. I kept 5% because 2% hurt `recency` (0.781) and I expect unseen traces to resemble that one in places.
